claims.text: A computational method incorporating machine-learning algorithms can generate more accurate potential-energy surfaces for multicomponent high-entropy alloys than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the many atomic configurations sampled by an ab initio liquid.
Improved machine-learned potential-energy surfaces will better represent atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Better representation of liquid atomic configurations will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference-target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method will improve predictions of material properties.
The proposed method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at or near their high melting temperatures.
Applicable composition and temperature ranges exist for high-entropy alloys, although those ranges are not specified.
The exact reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is uncertain.
Applicability of the proposed method to all high-entropy alloys is uncertain.
The proposed method can be tested by comparison with TOR-TILD's EAM references using thermodynamic-integration path mismatch and reference-target phase-space overlap.
Failure to show a significant improvement in configurational representation and path mismatch would falsify the hypothesis.
